title: AKS 1.32 is past its 12-month support window
summary: AKS 1.32 reached the end of its 12-month support window on 2026-03-31. Long-term support, which must be enabled for a cluster, ends on 2027-03-31.

sources.title: Supported Kubernetes versions in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

constraints: AKS upgrades one minor version at a time and upgrades the control plane before the agent pools.
Long-term support is opt-in per cluster; without it, a version stops receiving patches at the end of its 12-month support window.
An agent pool cannot run a newer version than its control plane, so raise the control plane and the pools together.

steps.title: Raise the cluster version
steps.instructions: Set kubernetes_version to the release in the replacement, then run terraform plan and apply the control-plane upgrade.

steps.title: Raise the agent pools
steps.instructions: Raise each azurerm_kubernetes_cluster_node_pool orchestrator_version so the agent pools match the new control plane.

steps.title: Remove APIs the new version deleted
steps.instructions: Read the Kubernetes deprecation guide for every minor version crossed and replace removed API versions in manifests and Helm charts before applying.

verification.purpose: Initialize without touching remote state and check that the configuration is valid.
Review the plan and confirm the control-plane and agent-pool changes are the intended ones.
Confirm the control plane reports the new version.
Confirm kubectl and the API server agree on the version.
